samples.summary: "the copies agree" test compares ciRunToRerun against a hand-retyped copy inside the test, not against the workflow's actual code
samples.evidence: checks.test.mjs:569-586 defines `const inline = (runs) => {...}` locally and then asserts `ciRunToRerun(fixture) === inline(fixture)` over six fixtures. That loop can never fail as a result of anything in agent-loop.yml / agent-rerun.yml changing — it only compares checks.mjs against a second copy of checks.mjs living in the test file. The only real link to the YAML is the two regexes at 559-560 (`r\.status === 'completed'`, `r\.id > n\.id`) plus the negative `for (const run of` check; a workflow edit such as `.filter((r) => r.status === 'completed' && r.conclusion === 'failure')` or a `.forEach`/`.sort()` rewrite still matches both regexes and the fixture loop, so the test named "the copies agree" passes while the copies have diverged. The behavior at stake (re-running the wrong or extra CI runs) is exactly what the comment says erodes the attempt bound and cancels the fixer mid-push.

samples.summary: The switch from per_page:1 to github.paginate(..., per_page:100) is untested — a revert to a truncated one-run listing would keep every assertion green
samples.evidence: The diff's substantive change at agent-loop.yml:156 and agent-rerun.yml (same block) is that the candidate list is now the FULL paginated set rather than the single newest run; the newest-COMPLETED rule is only meaningful over that full list. checks.test.mjs:547-564 greps the block for `r.status === 'completed'`, `r.id > n.id`, and one reRunWorkflow call, but asserts nothing about `github.paginate` or `per_page`. Reverting to `listWorkflowRuns({..., per_page: 1})` while keeping the filter/reduce would leave every assertion passing while the step silently stops finding the newest completed run whenever a newer in-flight run exists — the exact case checks.test.mjs:543 covers at the unit level.

samples.summary: The new `workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` gate in agent-iterate-ci.yml and ci-report.yml has no test, while the identical clause in agent-review-panel.yml does
samples.evidence: checks.test.mjs:168-219 evaluates the panel's gate expression and asserts it refuses `.github/workflows/pwn.yml`, and that the concurrency partition agrees. No equivalent exists for agent-iterate-ci.yml's gate (the arm that drives a `contents: write` fixer) or for ci-report.yml's `if:`. I grepped scripts/ for `agent-iterate-ci` and `ci-report` — the only hits are loop-status.test.mjs (latch literal), scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs (token/scripts/label assertions, not the `if:` gate), and comments. Deleting the path clause from either file would be silent: no lane fails, and the guard the diff's own comments describe as the thing that keeps a forged `name: CI` run from driving the fixer is gone.

samples.summary: gatherSignals' switch to path-based ciConclusion is untested — set-state.test.mjs only exercises the pure deriveState helper
samples.evidence: set-state.mjs:226-228 now derives `sig.ciConclusion` from `ciConclusion(runs)` (path-matched, and normalising cancelled/timed_out to "failure") instead of the old `r.name === "CI"` + created_at sort. grep of set-state.test.mjs for `ciConclusion|gatherSignals|workflow_runs` returns only deriveState fixtures (lines 83-99) that pass the signal in directly; nothing invokes gatherSignals or stubs the `actions/runs` response, so the new filtering/normalisation on this call site is covered only indirectly by checks.test.mjs's unit tests of ciConclusion. Impact is contained to lifecycle-label projection, but a wrong shape here (e.g. a run without `path`) would mislabel state with no test failing.

samples.summary: Mirror test bounds the workflow block by a fixed character window (at-200, at+700), so growth of the step can shift assertions off the code they mean to pin
samples.evidence: checks.test.mjs:557 `const block = yml.slice(at - 200, at + 700);` — the same fragility the diff explicitly fixed in mark-ready.test.mjs:418-423 by bounding on the following step rather than a character count. If the re-run block grows past 700 chars, the `r.id > n.id` / reRunWorkflow assertions can start matching (or miss) text belonging to a neighbouring step.
